QuestionStmt.S: If $f(x) = 2x^3 + mx^2 - 13x + n$ and 2, 3 are the roots of the equation $f(x) = 0$ then the value of $4m + 5n$ is

Solution.S:
$$ f(x) = 2x^3 + mx^2 - 13x + n $$

2, 3 are the roots of $f(x) = 0$.

$$\Rightarrow f(2) = 0$$
$$\Rightarrow 2(2)^3 + m(2)^2 - 13(2) + n = 0$$
$$\Rightarrow 16 + 4m - 26 + n = 0$$
$$\Rightarrow 4m + n = 10 \quad \cdots (i)$$

Also, $f(3) = 0$:

$$\Rightarrow 2(3)^3 + m(3)^2 - 13(3) + n = 0$$
$$\Rightarrow 54 + 9m - 39 + n = 0$$
$$\Rightarrow 9m + n = -15 \quad \cdots (ii)$$

Subtracting (i) from (ii):

$$5m = -25 \Rightarrow m = -5$$

Substituting $m = -5$ in (i):

$$4(-5) + n = 10 \Rightarrow n = 30$$

$$\therefore 4m + 5n = 4(-5) + 5(30) = -20 + 150 = 130$$

Thus the correct option is C: 130.
